export default "# Zhangye Danxia: China’s Rainbow Range\n\n![Zhangye Danxia Rainbow Mountains](/images/explore/zhangye-danxia.svg)\n\nGansu’s Zhangye Danxia National Geological Park feels like walking across a painter’s palette. Iron oxide, chlorite, and other mineral layers stacked over 24 million years create ridges that shift from terracotta to teal as clouds roll overhead. Since the Lanzhou–Xinjiang high-speed railway opened a direct stop at Zhangye West, it has never been easier to add the \"rainbow mountains\" to a Silk Road itinerary—provided you travel responsibly.\n\n## Orientation\n\n- **Nearest hub:** Zhangye city (airport code YZY, high-speed rail station \"Zhangye West\").\n- **Park zones:** Binggou, Sunan Yugu autonomous county, and the classic \"Colorful Hills\" core area.\n- **Best light:** Sunrise for saturated reds; golden hour after 7 p.m. for layered shadows.\n- **Climate note:** Summer temperatures reach 35 °C with intense UV; winter sees snow dusting that highlights rock striations.\n\n## Boardwalk Highlights\n\n1. **Platform 1 – Qicai Danxia:** First stop from the shuttle entrance; offers a panoramic sweep of layered ridgelines.\n2. **Platform 3 – Xianxia Terrace:** Faces west for dramatic sunset photos; telephoto lenses capture zebra-striped sandstone.\n3. **Platform 4 – Color Palette Valley:** Boardwalk descends closer to the textures—ideal for macro shots of mineral grains.\n4. **Binggou Stone Forest:** 18 km away, known for wind-carved spires reminiscent of Gothic cathedrals.\n\nLocal guide Yang Manlin suggests staggering visits over two days: *\"Spend day one photographing the main terraces, then return for a predawn hike in Binggou when the crowds have gone.\"*\n\n## Beyond the Park Gates\n\n### Sunan Yugu Cultural Stay\n\nThe ethnic Yugu community operates adobe guesthouses south of the park. Expect:\n\n- Handwoven carpets dyed with plant pigments mirroring Danxia colors.\n- Horseback rides along the Heihe River.\n- Workshops on Yugu throat singing and paper-cutting motifs featuring mountain silhouettes.\n\n### Gaoya Stargazing Base\n\nAstronomy clubs use the high plateau’s low light pollution to offer Milky Way nights. Powerful Dobsonian telescopes reveal Andromeda Galaxy arcs while photographers shoot light trails over the striped hills.\n\n## Practical Tips\n\n- **Tickets:** Purchase real-name tickets via the \"Zhangye Danxia\" mini program; peak-season entries are timed to protect fragile slopes.\n- **Transport:** Shuttle buses loop between four viewing areas every 10–15 minutes; private cars are not allowed past the gate.\n- **Drones:** Permits required; applications take 5 working days and must include flight plans to avoid wildlife zones.\n- **Weather:** Carry windproof layers even in summer; gusts funnel through valleys unexpectedly.\n\n## Responsible Travel Checklist\n\n| Action | Why it matters |\n| --- | --- |\n| Stay on boardwalks | Foot traffic erodes the mineral crust, dulling colors. |\n| Use refill stations | Single-use bottles often blow into ravines; refill taps are available at every platform. |\n| Support community guides | Fees fund bilingual signage and slope monitoring. |\n| Share real-time data | Upload photos of new cracks or rockfalls to park rangers via official WeChat. |\n\n## Sample 2-Day Itinerary\n\n**Day 1**\n- Morning arrival via high-speed rail, transfer to park.\n- Visit Platforms 1–4; sunset shoot at Platform 3.\n- Return to Zhangye city for hexi-style beef noodles.\n\n**Day 2**\n- Pre-dawn transfer to Binggou Stone Forest; hike the cliffside path (3 km).\n- Lunch in Sunan Yugu guesthouse, join dye workshop.\n- Evening stargazing at Gaoya base before overnight sleeper train to Dunhuang or Jiayuguan.\n\nZhangye Danxia rewards travelers who slow down and engage with the surrounding communities. When colors change every minute, patience is not only ethical—it’s the key to catching the park’s most unforgettable light.\n\n[Back to Explore](/#/explore)\n";
